title: Regulated Deployments — Concise Scripts for CISO and Audit Teams
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, sales-and-compliance-ready playbook with bite-sized scripts and technical talking points for conversations with CISOs, audit leads, and procurement teams evaluating private (VPC / on-prem) deployments of Redwood. Aim: enable reps and SEs to close regulated workloads faster by aligning on the minimal control-plane language the buyer needs to approve a pilot, and pre-empt common objections with short technical rebuttals.

Audience:
- Primary: Solutions Engineers, Sales Reps, Customer Security Engineers
- Secondary: Product marketing, legal pre-sales reviewers, GTM enablement

One-line elevator (for exec/VP-level buyers):
"Redwood Private gives you a managed inference runtime where customer data never leaves your network unless you explicitly opt in — control-plane operations can be fully delegated to your VPC or run via a narrow management channel with full auditability and KMS-backed key control."

Key themes to communicate (short bullets):
- Data residency: customer data and model inputs/outputs remain on customer infrastructure; metadata routing controls are explicit.
- Control plane options: managed control plane (minimal metadata, encrypted channel) OR customer-managed control plane (VPC-hosted control plane) depending on risk appetite.
- Zero-knowledge operations: optional telemetry-only health checks with sampling; no PII extraction in control messages.
- Key custody: native KMS/HSM integrations + bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options documented.
- Audit & compliance: full request-level audit logs, retention controls, and signed attestations for model version and rollout timelines.
- SLAs & failover: guaranteed fallback to pinned model variants and regional routing to maintain availability during incidents.

Recommended short scripts (use these verbatim or adapt):
- For CISO (concise):
  "We deploy Redwood as a customer-owned service inside your VPC; inference traffic and model state live on your network. The control plane can be set to customer-managed — that means config, rollouts, and telemetry never traverse Redwood-managed infrastructure. Where you want us to operate the control plane we limit payloads to non-sensitive telemetry and use end-to-end encrypted channels with keys you control. We provide audit logs and cryptographic attestations for every rollout and model change."

- For Audit Lead (concise):
  "We capture immutable, exportable logs of request IDs, model version, and decision timestamps. Log retention is configurable to match your retention policies; we can deliver logs to your SIEM/S3 with pre-signed, encrypted exports. We also provide a signed timeline for model changes to satisfy audit trails."

- For Procurement/Legal (pricing + risk):
  "Private deployments are licensed as a platform fee plus capacity; security obligations are contractually scoped — we offer SOC2 Type II evidence, ISO scope details, and an architecture annex that defines control plane responsibilities. For high-regulation customers we ship a private control-plane deployment with an annex that sets explicit operational ownership."

Common buyer objections and short rebuttals:
- Objection: "We can't have any vendor control plane touching our metadata."
  Rebuttal: "We offer a customer-managed control plane — the management APIs and configuration endpoints are hosted inside your VPC, behind your network controls and IAM. If you prefer our hosted control plane, we can restrict messages to heartbeat/health metadata only and use your KMS for encryption keys (BYOK)."

- Objection: "Telemetry could leak sensitive prompts or PII."
  Rebuttal: "Telemetry is opt-in and by default limited to performance counters and anonymized traces; request payloads are not collected. For customers that require it, we provide a proof-mode where sampling is disabled and any required debugging data is exchanged only via secure ticketed sessions under customer ops supervision."

- Objection: "How do we satisfy auditors on model provenance and changes?"
  Rebuttal: "We sign all model manifests and release artifacts; every rollout has a cryptographically verifiable record with deployer identity, timestamp, and byte-level checksum of model artifacts. We can deliver those artifacts and signatures as part of your audit package."

- Objection: "We need FIPS / HSM-backed key custody."
  Rebuttal: "Redwood integrates with KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and supports customer HSMs for private deployments. Key material can be generated and stored only in customer-controlled HSMs; the platform never has access to raw keys."

Competitive differentiation (talking points):
- Compared to cloud hosters' managed endpoints: Redwood provides the same developer ergonomics but with a deployment model that keeps model state and inference traffic on customer infrastructure and with explicit control-plane placement.
- Compared to self-hosted OSS runtimes: faster time to production — unified rollout, autoscaling, and SLO ops out of the box plus Redwood Optimize recommendations tuned for production economics.
- Compared to other private platform vendors: our default is an opinionated, observable runtime; customers get token-level cost visibility and per-route tracing that others typically don't provide for private installs.

Tech-precise language (one-liners engineers expect):
- "Control plane modes: (1) Redwood-managed minimal control plane (TLS+mutual auth, metadata-only), (2) Customer-managed control plane (runs in your VPC, API endpoints under your IAM), (3) Air‑gapped on-prem with periodic signed manifests."
- "Data plane: inference requests and KV cache never leave customer subnets unless you opt to mirror outputs for analytics; caching is local to the serving pool."
- "Keys: BYOK via KMS/HSM; key wrapping used for ephemeral node keys."
- "Audits: WORM logs, S3 delivery, and signed model manifests for provenance."

Sales tactic: pilot gating checklist (quick win to unblock procurement):
1) Agree pivot: pilot runs inside customer VPC with Redwood SE support for 4 weeks.
2) Deliver architecture annex (1–2 pages) defining control-plane mode, KMS choices, and log delivery.
3) Provide SOC2 artifact and short security questionnaire answer sheet.
4) Enable telemetry in 'ops-only' mode and ship debug activation playbook.
5) Produce a one-page audit package for the customer (signed manifests, sample logs, key control statement).

Example short email to CISO (template):
Subject: "Private inference pilot — control plane and data residency details"
Body: "Hi <Name>,
We can run the Redwood inference pilot inside your VPC and, per your preference, run the control plane under your network controls. Attached is a one-pager architecture annex that defines exactly which messages cross vendor boundaries, the KMS/HSM options, and the audit artifacts we'll provide. If agreeable, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our SE to map the pilot network egress and log routing. — Priya Singh"

Attachments & artifacts to carry to customer meetings:
- 1‑page architecture annex (template)
- Security questionnaire pre-filled (top 20 Qs)
- Example signed model manifest (anonymized)
- Log delivery sample (S3 + SIEM mapping)
- Short SOC2/ISO evidence pack

Open questions for product/legal (to resolve before scaling into enterprise sales):
- Minimum contract language for control plane responsibilities (we need an annex clause template)
- Template for HSM integration checklist (ops runbook)
- Default telemetry sampling policy for private installs (proposal: disabled by default, ops-enable only)

Short appendix (references and quick links):
- Confluence: Private Deployments overview and architecture (linked above)
- Jira: INFR-4123 (private control plane deploy templates)
- GH: ops-private-deployments repo (deployment manifests and example helm charts)

Notes on tone and length: keep responses short in customer threads — aim for 2–4 sentence technical points. Provide the annex early in the procurement process; auditors prefer concrete artifacts to abstract promises.

End of doc.
